subject: Private K8s deployment: site wiring, network segmentation & PV ownership (kickoff)
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@theramed.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private K8s deployment: site wiring, network segmentation & PV ownership (kickoff)

Oliver —

Thanks for the time today. Following up with a lightweight kickoff thread so we have a shared place for questions and the early artifacts. Goal: align on cluster footprint, VPC wiring & egress constraints, and persistent volume ownership (who mounts/owns PV lifecycle) before the Site Sprint (target: 2028-10-02).

High-level asks (please reply inline):
- Site footprint: expected node counts and GPU vs. CPU mix (we can accept ranges).
- Network: does your infrastructure team require egress via corporate NAT vs. dedicated egress IPs per tenant? Any IP allowlist windows we should know about?
- PV ownership: do you want Redwood to create & manage PVCs / PVs, or must customer ops pre-provision block volumes and hand off device paths?
- Encryption/KMS: which KMS will you use for LUKS keys (customer KMS or Redwood-managed envelope)?

Attachments: intake-checklist.pdf (initial runbook), pv-mapping.xlsx (blank template). I’ve also linked a draft network diagram (network-diagram-v1.png) in the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3c

Next steps: if we can get answers to the bullets by EOD Mon (9/17) we’ll lock the Site Sprint scope. If needed we can do a 30-min follow-up with your infra team.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: intake-checklist.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: pv-mapping.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Oliver Grant <oliver@theramed.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sabrina Li <sabrina.li@dataprac.io>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private K8s deployment: site wiring, network segmentation & PV ownership (kickoff)

Thanks Rachel —

Quick answers below, inline:
- Site footprint: initial pilot will be small: 3 control-plane hosts (non-GPU), 6 worker hosts: 2 x A100 nodes (GPU) and 4 x CPU-only for inference sidecars and side workloads. We may expand to 12 workers after validation.
- Network: we need egress to go through our corporate NATs for audit and per-subnet egress routing. We cannot accept dynamic public IPs from partners.
- PV ownership: preference is that our storage team pre-provisions block volumes; they want to keep billing and snapshots on our side. Redwood can drive PVC templates and mount logic, but not create the underlying block volumes.
- Encryption/KMS: we use an internal HashiCorp Vault-backed KMS and require customer-managed keys for host-level encryption.

Also: we’ll need to confirm audit logging — native kube-audit events must be forwarded to our Splunk cluster. Can Redwood provide a small audit-forwarder sidecar and configuration guidance?

I attached a short note from infra with constraints. Happy to jump on a quick call with our storage lead (Sabrina) next week.

Oliver
Head of Infrastructure, TheraMed Health
oliver@theramed.com
[Attachment: thera_infra_constraints.pdf (PDF)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver@theramed.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private K8s deployment: site wiring, network segmentation & PV ownership (kickoff)

Looping in security/ops notes — responding to Oliver inline:

On Fri, 14 Sep 2028 at 09:30, Oliver Grant <oliver@theramed.com> wrote:
> - Network: we need egress to go through our corporate NATs for audit and per-subnet egress routing. We cannot accept dynamic public IPs from partners.

We can support that. Implementation note: we will deploy the Redwood control-plane components in the tenant VPC but configure outbound via a customer-owned NAT gateway. We’ll require a small static egress CIDR for the control plane (to support third-party license/telemetry callbacks) — we can coordinate the exact /28 with TheraMed.

> - PV ownership: preference is that our storage team pre-provisions block volumes; they want to keep billing and snapshots on our side. Redwood can drive PVC templates and mount logic, but not create the underlying block volumes.

Agreed — we have two supported workflows: (A) Customer-provisioned PVs: customer creates block volumes, we provide PV manifests referencing the device path or volume ID. (B) Redwood-managed PVs: Redwood creates and manages underlying volumes via the cloud provider API. For TheraMed, choose option A. Action item: Sabrina to provide the storage provisioning playbook (volume naming, zone placement, snapshot cadence).

> - Encryption/KMS: we use an internal HashiCorp Vault-backed KMS and require customer-managed keys for host-level encryption.

We will support customer KMS for disk encryption. For Kubernetes-level secrets we recommend envelope encryption with a KMS integration; we can either call Vault via a sidecar or use an in-cluster KMS plugin. Action: Laura to capture KMS integration steps and run a short POC for secret encryption.

Audit logging: we can forward kube-audit to your Splunk. We usually install an audit-forwarder DaemonSet that ships to secure endpoints (TLS + mTLS). Sabrina, can you confirm the Splunk intake hostname/port and whether your team requires mutual TLS?

Security checks (preflight):
- RBAC baseline: we will ship a restricted RBAC policy for the Redwood control-plane components.
- Node isolation: kubelet TLS + node labels to avoid multi-tenant leakage.
- PV retention policy: define whether snapshots should be retained by TheraMed or Redwood.

I’ll produce a short security appendix and attach to the intake checklist by EOD.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@theramed.com>, Sabrina Li <sabrina.li@dataprac.io>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private K8s deployment: site wiring, network segmentation & PV ownership (kickoff)

Great — thanks everyone for the quick answers. Summary of decisions and next steps (action owners in parentheses):

1) Footprint: pilot = 3 control-plane hosts (Redwood-agentless control plane), 6 workers (2 GPU, 4 CPU). We’ll publish the target node selectors and tolerations for the A100 nodes. (Rachel)

2) Network & Egress: TheraMed will provide corporate NAT with static egress CIDR. Redwood needs the /28 for outbound callbacks and license telemetry; please share by Tue 9/19. (Oliver)

3) PV workflow: choose customer-provisioned PVs (TheraMed will create volumes; Redwood will supply PV manifests). Sabrina to share the provisioning playbook + sample naming convention by Wed 9/20. (Sabrina)

4) KMS & encryption: TheraMed KMS (Vault) accepted for host disk encryption. For in-cluster secret encryption we’ll run a short POC for KMS envelope integration next week. Laura will own the POC. (Laura)

5) Audit logging: Redwood will deploy the audit-forwarder DaemonSet configured to ship to your Splunk endpoint (mTLS optional). Need intake hostname/port and certificate requirements from Sabrina. (Irene / Sabrina)

6) Deliverables attached: network-diagram-v2.png (updated wiring), pv-mapping.xlsx (filled template, please review cell comments), intake-checklist.pdf (updated with security appendix). Links: HubSpot record HS-2345678, Drive folder https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3c

Please confirm the plan and we’ll lock the Site Sprint schedule. If there are no objections I’ll send a calendar invite for the preflight sync (30 min) on Thu 9/21 10:00 AM PT.

Thanks again,
Rachel Kim
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com
